title: Parliament begins final four sitting days
transcript:
Speaker 1: UN climate talks in Turkey have collapsed without a deal. That's after the European Union and others rejected the draft deal. After two weeks of tense negotiations, delegates deadlocked over whether to explicitly mention fossil fuels as the main driver of global warming. Major oil and gas producers, including Saudi Arabia, fiercely opposed the reference, leading to it being stripped from the final text. Co-hosts Turkey and Australia had been pledging with delegates to reach a consensus to keep the global climate fight on track. Chris Bowen said the transition away from fossil fuels is inevitable.
Speaker 2: Unfortunately, we're unable to reach agreement on a cover decision, as you know. And that's disappointing, very disappointing. An obvious issue is the transition away from fossil fuels, where some parties insisted that it must be mentioned. Other parties insisted that if it was mentioned, they would veto. The transition away from fossil fuels... in the real world is inevitable.
Speaker 3: It's happening.
Speaker 2: It's happening at speed and it's irreversible.
Speaker 1: UN officials have said that despite the deal collapsing, COP 31 has delivered real progress and concrete results. The talks have been suspended and will be reconvened next year. Close at home now, Canberra's final four sitting days will begin today as Labor tries to pass several key reforms before the Christmas break. The Albanese government is thought to be closer to a gas deal with the Coalition that's after promising a Western Australia carve-out. Elsewhere, a committee report into the digital duty of care has suggested bigger fines, a tech ombudsman and further gambling restrictions to duty of care legislation. Finally, an AI report is expected out of Parliament today, signalling where Labor sits on data centres, energy use and that all-important copyright issue too. That involves how exactly creatives are compensated when that is used to train the work of those AI models, a big sticking point at the moment when it comes to the growth at a rapid rate of artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence will be recognised as a major foreign policy and national security challenge. Foreign Minister Penny Wong set to use a speech this week to warn that the evolving technology gives foreign actors new tools to undermine democracies. Many people concerned Australian AI data centres could be vulnerable to foreign actors. Australian musicians could face a legal battle with some of the world's biggest AI firms. The foreign policy speech to be given in Parliament tomorrow. The New South Wales opposition has vowed to raise maths standards for students across the state if they win next year's state election. The state's shadow education minister, James Wallace, announcing a $ 50 million investment to improve NAPLAN numeracy results with the goal of reaching 90% proficiency.
Speaker 3: I don't want to accept a reality where a third of our kids aren't able to do maths to the expectations we have under the curriculum. We're going to try to boost them to get them back to the level we expect.
Speaker 1: The program will also include five new maths hubs at leading schools and mandatory timetable checks for Year 4 students. There's a growing trend of crime bosses live streaming violent acts to ensure their instructions are undertaken. That's according to the New South Wales Crime Commission, which revealed that the use of Airbnb-style rentals as safe houses and staging points for murders and kidnappings are among growing trends too. Now, the commission says it has frozen $ 168 million in criminal assets last financial year alone. A Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad was set on fire in a drone strike in the Gulf of Finland. That's according to the Finnish Defence Ministry. The sanctioned vessel was struck in international waters before it drifted into Finnish territorial waters while on fire. Finland's prime minister said war is spilling over into our immediate vicinity. Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor. Two Russian cruise missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in southeastern Poland early on Friday. A meeting of NATO's North Atlantic Council set to be held in Brussels today to discuss the violation of Polish airspace by Russian missiles.
